Public consumer fixtures for the Dokploy Compose environment qualification.

create-env-file.ts is the unmodified getCreateEnvFileCommand export from:
https://github.com/Dokploy/dokploy/blob/073713f0b863eca4285ad24db00550af1b39397a/packages/server/src/utils/builders/compose.ts

prepare-environment.ts is the unmodified prepareEnvironmentVariables,
prepareEnvironmentVariablesForFile and parseEnvironmentKeyValuePair exports from:
https://github.com/Dokploy/dokploy/blob/073713f0b863eca4285ad24db00550af1b39397a/packages/server/src/utils/docker/utils.ts

These are Dokploy v0.30.10 source excerpts, used under Apache-2.0:
https://github.com/Dokploy/dokploy/blob/073713f0b863eca4285ad24db00550af1b39397a/LICENSE.MD
Copyright 2026-present Dokploy Technology, Inc.
The Apache-2.0 license text is in LICENSE.

dotenv/main.cjs and package.json are unmodified dotenv v16.4.5 sources:
https://github.com/motdotla/dotenv/blob/v16.4.5/lib/main.js
https://github.com/motdotla/dotenv/blob/v16.4.5/package.json
The MIT license and copyright notice are in dotenv/LICENSE.

consume.mjs supplies dependencies to the original functions, removes TypeScript
types with Node's built-in stripper, and executes the generated file command
inside the test's temporary directory. No network, provider or application
containers are used. Docker Compose is provisioned from the repository CI's
single version declaration; it is not vendored here.

legacy-literal.env is a synthetic saved record from Launchplane's previous
Compose codec. It proves that reading and rewriting old provider records keeps
their logical inputs while delivering them through the current provider.
